top_issues: Pot belly is missing: the light-green belly is a flat bib slab on the chest, and the belt sits under it instead of the belly hanging over it
The arms stop at mid-thigh, not the knees, and the hands are mitts with claw spikes rather than three fingers; the nose is a straight wedge beak, not a hooked nose
The buckle is a flat cream square, off-palette and not chunky; seen from the side (az090) the back loincloth is thin strap slivers (4 slivers on loin_back)
A.brief_fit: Reads as a goblin (domed head, horizontal ears, yellow eyes, fanged grin), but pot belly, knee-length arms and hooked nose are weak or missing.

top_issues: The head is a boxy dog-like muzzle, not a hooked nose, and the back of the skull (back34) has a recessed vertical groove that reads as a modelling error
The mouth seam is a dark crease wrapping the jaw, with a sliver line flagged at the jaw hinge; the far ear is extremely long and blade-thin in hero and az090
The side loincloth panels are thin plates (slivers in az090 and back34); the belly is a shaded chest panel with no pot over the belt
B.brief_fit: Has the right parts (arms to the knees, chunky gold buckle, long ears, fangs), but the head reads as a snouted dog-goblin and the face lacks a heavy brow.

top_issues: The eyes are flat hexagon decals on the cheek plane, with no brow ridge overhanging them, so the face reads a little blank
The buckle is a pale grey block, off-palette; the side loincloth strips are paper-thin sticks in az090 (sliver flags)
There is a posed fold-over at the right shoulder/neck junction (purple on the az000 heatmap), and the ear tips are needle-thin slivers
C.brief_fit: Closest to the brief: big domed head, hooked nose, wide fanged grin, long horizontal ears, pot belly over the belt, arms to the knees, and clear three-fingered hands and three-toed feet.

goblin.why: C is the only one with the hooked nose, the pot belly over the belt and knee-length arms all in the base silhouette; A is clean but generic, and B's snouted head and grooved skull break its identity.

top_issues: The body is a straight cylinder with uniform horizontal ring bands, not an egg; the head is a hard-cornered box
The legs are bare cream stilts with no feathering, and the wings are flat dark slabs stuck to the sides
The facial disc has no dark rim and the cream belly is washed out; the attack frame's feet splay into broken shards
A.brief_fit: Reads as a horned owl from the front with the best eyes, but the egg body, feathered legs and disc rim are missing.

top_issues: The brows are rectangular sticks that jut past the head silhouette in hero and the head close-up, reading as glued-on planks
The facial disc is a square mask with no dark rim; the tan chest band adds an off-palette colour
The eye rings are flat octagons with a visible stepped inset in the wire, and the tail fan is a thin plate (sliver on the tail underside in az090)
B.brief_fit: Good match: egg body, folded wings with a fan tail, big orange eyes, tufts, feathered brown thighs and dark talons.

top_issues: The near brow is a spike that projects off the face like a third horn (hero, head close-up)
The eyes are small for 'big round eyes', and the talons are pale beak-colour spiky toe fans that read as splinters, not dark talons
The wing seam shows a hard stepped edge along the flank (az090), and the disc is rectangular
C.brief_fit: Good anatomy with a dark disc rim and V brows, but the eyes are undersized and the feet and talons miss the brief.

owl.why: B has the big eyes, egg body, feathered legs and dark talons together; C loses on small eyes and splinter feet, and A on its ring-banded cylinder body and stilt legs.

top_issues: The folded wings are boxy slabs on the back and read as shoulder pads from the front (az000); the finger spars barely show
Values are near-uniform blue-black, so the planes go muddy; the thighs are blocky boxes
There is almost no S-curve in the neck, the dorsal spines are tiny, and the attack pose does not mantle the wings
A.brief_fit: Reads as a compact bird-dragon/griffin with a good raven head and amber eye, but the wings-as-forelimbs wyvern cue is weak.

top_issues: The head is a blocky helmet with a tiny hexagon eye; the hackles are thin black splinter shards
The wings are rigid straight sticks with triangular membrane plates and no tapered finger spars; slivers are flagged along the wing leading edges
Very dark values flatten the body, and the attack lunges only the head, with no wing mantle
B.brief_fit: The strongest wyvern read: wing-forelimbs with thumb claws planted, S-neck, graded spines, a long tail with a fin, and swept horns.

top_issues: The wings are a single purple cape plate hung on each flank, with no wing arm, spars or thumb claw, so the wyvern identity fails
The chest and neck are covered in dozens of needle-thin hackle shards that splinter at close range
The body is an upright raven with no neck S-curve and no wing mantle in the attack
C.brief_fit: Reads as a horned raven with a dragon tail; the brief's first requirement (a wyvern whose wings are the forelimbs) is not met.

raven_wyvern.why: B is the only one whose base silhouette reads wyvern-first (wing-forelimbs, S-neck, long finned tail); A reads as a griffin and C as a caped raven.
